items.title: Greedy radius growth after repair
items.spec: After _repair returns a valid packing, make one growth pass: for each circle in random order (rng from seed), set its radius to the largest value that keeps it inside the square and clear of all other circles given their current radii, i.e. r_i = min(wall distance, min_j(d_ij - r_j)). Repeat the pass until the total sum stops increasing by more than 1e-12, at most 5 passes. Then subtract SHRINK as before. This recovers slack left by the pairwise shrink, especially around rattlers, and does not change the SLSQP stage.

items.title: Per-stage SLSQP iteration budget
items.spec: Give each cap stage its own maxiter instead of MAX_ITER=200 everywhere. Use a small budget (about 60) for the caps 0.05 to 0.2, where the packing is still moving a lot and a rough answer is enough, and a larger budget (about 400) for the caps 0.3, 0.36, 0.4 and the uncapped final stage. Keep the same cap list. The aim is to spend the restart's CPU time where the final sum is decided, which gives more restarts per call.

items.title: Loose tolerance early, tight tolerance late
items.spec: Pass ftol to SLSQP that depends on the stage: 1e-4 for the caps below 0.2, 1e-6 for the middle caps, and 1e-10 for the final uncapped stage. Keep the iteration cap as it is. Early stages only need to place the circles roughly, and the tight final stage fixes the sum. Each restart should finish sooner, so more restarts fit in the 80 percent budget.

items.title: Geometric cap grid near the final radius scale
items.spec: Replace the linear cap grid np.arange(0.05, 0.4, 0.02) plus 1.0 with a geometric grid from 0.05 up to 0.2, then a linear grid from 0.2 to 0.4 with step 0.01, then 1.0. Radii of the 26-circle optimum are around 0.08 to 0.2, so most of the continuation should be spent in that band. Keep everything else unchanged.

items.title: Native SLSQP bounds for the box and radius limits
items.spec: Move the box and nonnegativity limits out of the constraint vector and into the bounds argument of minimize. Centre coordinates get bounds (0, 1) and radii get bounds (0, cap) for each stage. Keep only the pair-distance constraints in the constraint list, and keep the cap as a bound rather than a constraint row. This shrinks the number of constraint rows from about 6n + n(n-1)/2 to n(n-1)/2, which speeds each SLSQP iteration. The optimum is unchanged.

items.title: Freeze circles that hit the cap
items.spec: At the end of each cap stage, find circles whose radius equals the current cap within 1e-6. Remove their radii from the optimisation variables and hold them at that radius for the next stage. Only free circles keep their pair constraints against each other. This reduces the dimension of each SLSQP call as the continuation proceeds. Unfreeze everything for the final uncapped stage so the optimum is still found over all circles.

items.title: Nearest-neighbour radius prior at initialisation
items.spec: Instead of setting every initial radius to INIT_RADIUS=0.05, compute the initial centres first, then set each initial radius to 0.5 times the distance to its nearest other start centre, further capped at the wall distance and at 0.15. Keep the random centres drawn from the same rng. This gives a feasible-looking start with radii matched to local spacing, with no extra random draws.

items.title: Feasibility guard on stage acceptance
items.spec: After each SLSQP stage, check the returned iterate for feasibility: all pair constraints and wall constraints at least -1e-9 and the sum of radii finite. If the stage's result is infeasible or res.status indicates a failure, keep the previous stage's feasible x rather than the failed iterate. Use the previous x for the next stage. This stops an unstable SLSQP stage from pushing a bad start into later caps and from being selected as best.

items.title: Sort circles by initial radius before SLSQP
items.spec: After drawing the random start, reorder the circles so that the largest initial radii come first, and then run the whole continuation in that order. Sorting is done only once per restart and changes no constraint. Because SLSQP's pivoting depends on variable order, this gives a different path through the same problem and is cheap to try. Apply the inverse permutation to the returned centres and radii so the harness sees the original order.

items.title: Random-order repair with max-overlap ties
items.spec: In _repair, instead of picking the single largest overlap each step, scan the pairs in a random order from the seed's rng and fix every overlapping pair in that order by proportional shrink, looping until no overlap remains or 200 passes are used. Break ties at random. This changes which circles absorb the shrink and can keep more total radius than the greedy largest-overlap rule, with no change to the optimiser.

items.title: Final tight-tolerance SLSQP polish of best
items.spec: After the restart loop ends, take the best packing (before repair) and run one more SLSQP from it with cap=1.0, maxiter=500 and ftol=1e-12, using the same constraints. Reserve about 1.5 s of CPU for it by lowering the loop's time check accordingly (for example stop restarts at 0.75*time_limit). Accept the polished result only if it is better after _repair. Keep the rest unchanged.

items.title: Finer cap continuation schedule
items.spec: Change the cap schedule in _solve_once from np.arange(0.05, 0.4+1e-9, 0.02) to a finer grid np.arange(0.06, 0.30+1e-9, 0.03) followed by a few steps 0.35, 0.45 and then 1.0, and cut MAX_ITER per stage to 100. The goal is more restarts at the same quality. Keep everything else unchanged.

items.title: Dihedral images of the best as restart seeds
items.spec: After the first 5 plain restarts, on every third restart start SLSQP (with the cap continuation starting at cap=0.4 then 1.0 only) from a random one of the 8 dihedral images of the best packing's centres and radii, with small Gaussian noise (sd 0.01) on the centres. Keep the best result by sum of radii after repair.

items.title: Squared-distance pair constraints
items.spec: In cons, replace the sqrt pair constraint with the smooth form d2 - (r_i+r_j)^2 where d2 is the squared centre distance, clipping r sums at nonnegative values via the existing r>=0 constraints. This removes the non-smooth sqrt at zero distance. Keep the cap continuation and everything else the same.

items.title: Adaptive per-restart iteration budget
items.spec: In _solve_once, stop a cap stage early when the sum of radii improved by less than 1e-5 relative to the previous stage, and skip straight to cap=1.0. Set the per-stage maxiter to 120 for the early stages and 300 for the last. This saves CPU for more restarts. Keep other code unchanged.

items.title: Alternating LP radii and SLSQP centres polish
items.spec: For the best packing at the end, alternate up to 5 times: fix the centres and solve the radii exactly with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS) maximising sum r subject to r_i+r_j<=d_ij and wall constraints; then run a short SLSQP (maxiter 50) over all variables from that point. Keep the result if the repaired sum improves. Use about 1 s of reserved CPU time.

items.title: Centre jitter between continuation stages
items.spec: In _solve_once, after each cap stage except the last, add Gaussian noise with sd 0.003 to the centres (clipped to [0.02, 0.98]) and shrink the radii by 3 percent before the next stage. This helps escape jammed states. Seed everything from rng.

items.title: Log-sum-exp soft pair constraints early
items.spec: For the first 4 cap stages, replace the pair constraints with the soft version d_ij - r_i - r_j >= -0.01 so early stages allow slight overlap; the later stages use the exact constraints. This smooths early continuation. Implement by adding a margin parameter to cons that is 0.01 for the early stages and 0 for the rest.

items.title: Radius-ordering symmetry breaking
items.spec: Add inequality constraints r[k] >= r[k+1] for k in 0..n-2 to the SLSQP constraint vector in cons, only for the cap stages, and sort the initial radii in descending order. This removes permutation symmetry among circles. Drop the ordering constraints in the last stage (cap=1.0) so the final optimum is unrestricted.

items.title: Square-grid-with-defects starts
items.spec: For a random third of the restarts, build the start as a 5x5 grid of centres at spacing 0.2 offset by 0.1, add one extra centre at a random location, jitter all centres with Gaussian noise sd 0.03, and use initial radius 0.08. Other restarts stay uniform random. The cap continuation is applied as before.

items.title: Coarser cap ladder for more restarts
items.spec: In _solve_once, replace the cap list list(np.arange(0.05, 0.4 + 1e-9, 0.02)) + [1.0] with list(np.arange(0.05, 0.4 + 1e-9, 0.05)) + [1.0], so there are 8 capped stages instead of 18, followed by the free stage. Change nothing else. Each restart becomes much cheaper, so more random restarts fit in the same TIME_FRACTION of the budget. This tests whether the gain from the continuation comes from having stages at all rather than from small steps.

items.title: Split SLSQP iteration budget: short capped stages, long free stage
items.spec: In _solve_once, pass options={'maxiter': 40} to minimize for every capped stage (cap < 1.0) and options={'maxiter': 400} for the final cap=1.0 stage. Write it as maxiter = 400 if cap >= 1.0 else 40 inside the loop. The capped stages only need to steer the packing roughly. The final stage gets enough iterations to converge fully, and the restarts are cheaper overall.

items.title: Second fresh free SLSQP stage per restart
items.spec: In _solve_once, after the cap loop finishes, call minimize once more with the same objective, the cap=1.0 constraint function, method SLSQP and maxiter MAX_ITER, starting from x. Then set x = res.x and return as before. Restarting SLSQP clears its BFGS Hessian approximation and its line-search state, which often lets it get a little further than a solver that has stalled. This adds a single extra stage and changes nothing else.

items.title: Stack perimeter-ring start with power-law radius start
items.spec: Combine the two best near-incumbent changes (slots 28 and 16). In _solve_once, on a random half of the restarts (rng.random() < 0.5), place the centres as in slot 28. That means about 4*sqrt(n) circles on a ring near the border (jittered positions at distance about 0.1 from the edges, evenly spaced along the perimeter), with the rest uniform in [0.25, 0.75]^2. On all restarts, set the initial radii to a shuffled power-law profile: r_k proportional to k^-0.5 for k=1..n, scaled so the mean is INIT_RADIUS, then randomly permuted with rng. Keep the cap continuation unchanged. Use rng for all randomness.

items.title: Per-circle heterogeneous radius caps
items.spec: In the cap continuation, give each circle its own cap instead of one shared cap. At the start of each restart, draw weights w = rng.permutation(np.linspace(0.6, 1.4, n)). In capped stages, replace the constraint cap - r with cap * w - r, where cap runs over the same ladder 0.05..0.4. Keep the final cap=1.0 stage unchanged, so its constraint is 1.0 - r. This breaks the size symmetry in the early stages, so that some circles are encouraged to grow large and others to stay small. That size mix is what good 26-circle packings have.

items.title: Cap-reheat of the incumbent
items.spec: In solve, once a best packing exists, run half the restarts (rng.random() < 0.5) as reheats instead of random starts. Start from the best centres plus Gaussian noise with sd 0.02, clipped to [0.05, 0.95]. Set all radii to 0.05. Then run the full radius-cap continuation from that start (pass the start vector to _solve_once through an optional x0 argument). The other half stay uniform random restarts. Unlike plain perturbation, this lets the circles regrow their sizes from scratch while keeping the incumbent's spatial layout.

items.title: Wider centre spread and smaller initial radii
items.spec: Change the settings INIT_LOW from 0.1 to 0.03 and INIT_RADIUS from 0.05 to 0.02. Change nothing else. Starting centres then cover nearly the whole square, including the border bands where many circles in good packings sit. The smaller initial radii start below the first cap of 0.05, so the first capped stage does real growth work instead of starting at the cap.

items.title: Geometric cap ladder with fine early steps
items.spec: In _solve_once, replace the cap list with list(0.04 * 1.15 ** np.arange(17)) + [1.0], about 0.04 rising to roughly 0.38 in 17 steps. Steps are fine where the caps are small and the topology is decided, and coarse near the top where most constraints are already inactive. The number of stages stays close to the current 18, so the cost per restart is about the same.

items.title: Move box, cap and nonnegativity constraints into SLSQP bounds
items.spec: In _solve_once, drop the box constraints c-r, 1-c-r? No: keep the four centre-minus-radius wall constraints, but remove the r >= 0 and cap - r entries from cons. Instead pass bounds to minimize: centres in [0, 1] and radii in [0, cap] for each stage (bounds=[(0,1)]*2n + [(0,cap)]*n). SLSQP handles bounds natively and more cheaply than general inequalities. This removes 2n constraint rows per stage and makes each iteration faster, with the same feasible set.

items.title: Annealed overlap allowance during the cap continuation
items.spec: In _solve_once, let the pair constraints in capped stages be d - r_i - r_j + eps >= 0, where eps starts at 0.01 at the first cap and decreases linearly to 0 at the last capped stage (cap 0.4). The final cap=1.0 stage uses eps = 0, so the constraints are exact, and the repair step is unchanged. Allowing a slight overlap early lets circles slide past each other while the structure forms, which avoids early jamming. Only the pair constraints get eps; the wall constraints stay exact.

items.title: Coarser cap schedule for more restarts
items.spec: In _solve_once, change the cap list from np.arange(0.05, 0.4 + 1e-9, 0.02) + [1.0] (19 stages) to a coarser one: [0.05, 0.08, 0.11, 0.14, 0.18] + [1.0] (6 stages). Keep everything else identical. The aim is roughly three times as many restarts in the same CPU time while keeping the continuation effect in the radius range that matters (optimal radii lie around 0.07 to 0.14). Put the list in a module-level constant CAPS so it is easy to tune.

items.title: Truncated dense cap schedule in the active radius range
items.spec: In _solve_once, replace the cap list with one that is dense only where caps are active and drops the inactive upper part: caps = list(np.arange(0.06, 0.14 + 1e-9, 0.01)) + [1.0] (9 capped stages plus the free stage). Caps above about 0.15 bind almost no circle in a 26-circle packing, so the stages from 0.15 to 0.39 are wasted solves. Keep MAX_ITER, the objective, the constraints and the repair unchanged. Store the list in a module-level constant CAPS.

items.title: Skip cap stages that are not binding
items.spec: In the cap loop of _solve_once, before calling minimize for a cap below 1.0, check whether the cap would bind: if the current radii satisfy x[2*n:].max() < cap - 1e-6 and at least one stage has already been solved, skip all remaining capped stages and go straight to the final free stage (cap = 1.0). Implement with a simple `if cap < 1.0 and solved and x[2*n:].max() < cap - 1e-6: continue`. This removes the redundant SLSQP solves at high caps where the previous solution is already a local optimum, so more restarts fit in the time budget. No other change.

items.title: Short capped stages, long final free stage
items.spec: Give the continuation stages unequal SLSQP iteration budgets. Replace the single MAX_ITER with two constants: STAGE_ITER = 40 for every capped stage (cap < 1.0) and FINAL_ITER = 600 for the last free stage (cap = 1.0). In the loop pass options={'maxiter': STAGE_ITER if cap < 1.0 else FINAL_ITER}. The capped stages only need to move the configuration roughly; the final stage should run to true convergence instead of stopping at 200 iterations. Keep the cap list, the constraints and the repair unchanged.

items.title: Radius limits as SLSQP bounds instead of constraints
items.spec: Remove the last two blocks (r and cap - r) from the constraint vector in cons, so it returns only the pair distances and the four wall blocks. Pass the radius limits natively through the bounds argument of minimize: bounds = [(0, 1)] * (2 * n) + [(0, cap)] * n for each stage (for the final stage use cap = 1.0, i.e. effectively free). Before each stage clip the warm-start radii into [0, cap] so the start respects the bounds. This removes 52 nonlinear-treated constraints from each SLSQP QP subproblem and keeps the centres inside the square exactly, making every restart cheaper and the cap handling exact. Keep the cap list and the repair unchanged.

items.title: Three-way mixture of the near-win restart types
items.spec: Stack the three changes that each scored slightly better than the incumbent. Give _solve_once an optional argument x0 and let solve choose the start type for each restart with the seeded rng: (a) with probability 1/4 the plain uniform start; (b) with probability 1/4 a perimeter-ring start: about 16 centres evenly spaced along a square ring at distance 0.1 from the walls with Gaussian jitter of sd 0.02, the remaining centres uniform in [0.25, 0.75]^2, radii INIT_RADIUS; (c) with probability 1/4 a uniform centre start whose radii follow a shuffled power-law profile, r_k proportional to k^-0.5 for k = 1..n, rescaled to mean INIT_RADIUS and clipped to [0.02, 0.1]; (d) with probability 1/4, once a best packing exists, an affine-strain shake of the best centres: map c to 0.5 + (c - 0.5) @ A with A = I + E, E a random 2x2 matrix with entries N(0, 0.05), clip to [0.05, 0.95], radii reset to INIT_RADIUS (before a best packing exists use type a). All starts then run the unchanged radius-cap continuation and repair.

items.title: Melt and regrow the incumbent through the cap continuation
items.spec: Add a second restart type that reuses the continuation as the perturbation. After the first restart, on every other loop iteration take the best packing's centres, add Gaussian jitter of sd 0.01 (clip to [0.02, 0.98]), set all radii to min(r_best, MELT_CAP) with MELT_CAP drawn uniformly from [0.07, 0.11] with the seeded rng, and run the cap continuation only from MELT_CAP upward (caps in the existing list that are >= MELT_CAP, then 1.0). To support this, give _solve_once optional arguments x0 and cap_min. Because the big circles are deflated and regrown while the small ones stay, the packing can rearrange locally without losing its global structure. Keep the result if its repaired sum of radii beats the best. The other half of the iterations remain plain random restarts.

items.title: Stage-level racing of restarts
items.spec: Abandon unpromising restarts in the middle of the cap continuation. Keep in solve a list of the sum of radii that each earlier restart had right after a fixed checkpoint stage (the stage with cap closest to 0.11) and pass it to _solve_once. After that checkpoint stage, compute the current sum of radii; if at least 6 earlier values are recorded and the current value is below their median, return None immediately (solve then skips repair and comparison for that restart); in every case append the value to the list. Restarts that pass continue through the remaining caps and the free stage as now. This spends about half the late-stage SLSQP time only on the better half of the starts. Everything else unchanged.

items.title: Explore then exploit time split
items.spec: Split the time budget into two phases in solve. For the first 55 percent of time_limit run the plain random restarts exactly as now. From then until TIME_FRACTION * time_limit, run only exploitation restarts from the best packing: take the best centres, apply a random affine strain c -> 0.5 + (c - 0.5) @ (I + E) with E a 2x2 matrix of N(0, 0.04) entries plus per-centre Gaussian jitter of sd 0.005, clip to [0.05, 0.95], reset radii to INIT_RADIUS, and run the full unchanged cap continuation (give _solve_once an optional x0 argument). Replace the best whenever the repaired sum of radii improves, so later shakes start from the new best. All randomness from the seeded rng.

items.title: Geometric cap schedule from a feasible small start
items.spec: Change the continuation so it starts nearly feasible and grows the cap by a constant ratio. Set INIT_RADIUS = 0.02 and replace the cap list with a geometric sequence: cap_0 = 0.03, cap_{k+1} = 1.18 * cap_k while cap <= 0.16 (about 11 stages), followed by the free stage cap = 1.0. With small initial radii the random start has few overlaps, so the first SLSQP stages are cheap and the circles settle into a spread-out arrangement before they compete; the geometric spacing puts more stages at small caps where the topology is decided and fewer at large caps. Keep MAX_ITER, the constraints and the repair unchanged.
